chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who gifts herself to a man, or her guardian gifts her to him, he said: 'No, that was for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and it is not for others except if he compensates her with something, little or much.'

key_terms.وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا: She gifted herself (gave herself in marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman gives herself to a man in marriage without a specified dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the unique prerogative of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his successors, who could accept a woman's self-gift without material compensation, versus the general rule for others requiring a dowry (mahr). It highlights the theological concept of 'khulus' (dedication) in early Islamic jurisprudence, where the Prophet's spiritual authority allowed for non-monetary marital unions, a practice not automatically extended to the general community. This ruling underscores the flexibility of early marriage contracts while affirming the necessity of consideration (mahr) for ordinary believers.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a woman who gifts herself to a man, or her guardian gifts her to him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, that was for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and it is not for others except if he were to place something to be for her, be it little or more’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain persons of his people from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “About the case of a woman who gifts herself or her guardian gifts her to a man, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘No, it was only for the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and not for others unless it is in exchange for something, little or more.’”
